scope: Complete source-linked pureTV assembly plus ten explicit analytic test-bench parts; only checked source interfaces and nominal sampled actuation are claimed.

findings.detail: All nine actual GLBs preserve measured spring endpoints and physical contact surfaces within 0.001 mm; this is separate from collision coverage.

report.scope: Rendered source spring endpoints and physical contact surfaces match measured calibration within 0.001 mm; collision/path evidence is separate.

findings.detail: All recorded rest and sampled source-motion candidates are accounted for, including explicit local contact interfaces.

method.geometry: Every evaluated source triangle, no decimation or display GLB used
method.broadPhase: All object pairs at rest, and each active group against every source object at each pose; AABB pruning only
method.containmentTest: Three non-axis oriented exit-minus-entry ray counts agree; exact float64 triangle-plane/edge tests exclude surface points; complete float64 grid/ray fallback resolves disagreeing BVH votes; no nearest-normal-only conclusion
method.componentCoverage: Blender native Mesh Island field provides a representative for every connected source component, additional nearby vertices and intersecting-face centroids sampled bidirectionally
method.motion: Caps, ABXY labels and remaining upper spring seats move -Z; springs compress around fixed lower plane; switch actuators move max(0,stroke-pretravel) in -Z
limitations: Discrete poses are not continuous collision detection.
Bounded containment/depth witnesses are not complete maximum-penetration or manufacturing-clearance measurements.
Open or inconsistent topology is never treated as a reliable containment target.
Unclassified contact is unknown, never a pass; exact pair plus bounded local design interface is required.
Different-key moving members additionally use independent pairwise stroke Cartesian products; interpolation between listed samples is not certified.

Spring geometry uses the application's affine axial display compression. Wire cross-section preservation, spring solid length and force require the separate spring specification; this source-envelope audit is not a spring material simulation.
Every harness object also receives a mandatory exact source self-intersection check. Self-intersection of other objects and manufacturing defects remain outside this inter-object audit scope.
Material stiffness, friction, tolerance distribution and electrical connectivity are not established by this mesh audit.

findings.detail: Ten analytic bench geometries passed actual MCP proxy checks and are strictly AABB-separated from every unsimplified source object's complete axial swept bounds.

checks.detail: Every final source, display hash and source object matches the complete exported workbench assembly.
All nine actual GLBs preserve measured spring endpoints and physical contact surfaces within 0.001 mm; this is separate from collision coverage.
All recorded rest and sampled source-motion candidates are accounted for, including explicit local contact interfaces.
Nine source internal moving/elastic groups checked along the calibrated stroke.
Eight sleeve locks and the confirmation key's actual mounting/guide/retention interfaces have checked source evidence.
Actual workbench MCP exercised all nine approach/contact/release branches, real renderer motion and the ten analytic bench entities.
Ten analytic bench geometries passed actual MCP proxy checks and are strictly AABB-separated from every unsimplified source object's complete axial swept bounds.

limitations: Source collision/clearance evidence is limited to recorded discrete poses and bounded containment witnesses, not continuous collision detection or manufacturing certification.
Spring stiffness, mass, damping and switch overtravel are the declared nominal calibration assumptions, not measured material/fatigue/friction certification.
Spring collision poses use the declared runtime model's axial scaling of the source mesh; constant-wire-section helix deformation and wire self-contact are not solved.

Mesh self-intersection checks cover every harness object; other source objects are covered by the recorded inter-object/interface audits, not a general self-intersection or manufacturing-defect certificate.
Nine lamps and one power source are an external analytic test bench; logical wires do not certify manufactured insulation, solder joints or ESP32 firmware.

Lock/mount trajectories cover named mating pairs in their reported open-housing assembly sequence; they do not certify inserting assembled modules into a closed shell or all-component maintenance sweeps.

The declared compliant lock pads undergo substantial nominal compression during insertion. Allowable pad strain, nonlinear stiffness, assembly force and service life have not been measured; rigid path clearance is not a pad material certification.
